task: Restart a Deployment in the correct namespace
user_request: Restart the checkout-api pods, they're stuck.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api` without a `-n/--namespace` flag, so it executed against the current context's `default` namespace where no such deployment exists, then reported success from a stale prior command.
failure_type: Omitted namespace selector
root_cause: The deployment lives in namespace `payments`, but the command omitted `-n payments`; kubectl defaulted to `default` and returned a NotFound that the agent did not surface.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the active kube namespace was already `payments`. Wrong because the kubeconfig context defaults to `default`. Avoidable by running `kubectl config view --minify` or always passing `-n payments` explicitly.
impact: Stuck checkout pods kept failing readiness for another 15 minutes while the operator believed a restart had been issued.
correct_action: Run `kubectl -n payments rollout restart deployment/checkout-api` and confirm rollout status in that namespace.
recovery_plan: Run `kubectl config view --minify` to read the default namespace
Re-issue the restart with `-n payments`
Watch `kubectl -n payments rollout status deployment/checkout-api`
Confirm pods reach Ready
Add namespace to the runbook command
evaluation_criteria: Checks every namespaced kubectl call includes an explicit namespace
Verifies the agent confirmed the resource exists in the target namespace
Detects success claimed without checking command exit

task: Run a cost-bounded BigQuery scan
user_request: Count events in the analytics.events table for last month.
agent_action: Agent submitted `bigquery.jobs.query` selecting from `analytics.events` with no `WHERE _PARTITIONDATE` filter and no `maximum_bytes_billed` set, scanning the entire 9 TB partitioned table.
failure_type: Omitted partition filter / byte cap
root_cause: The table is date-partitioned; the query omitted the partition-pruning predicate and the job config omitted `maximum_bytes_billed`, so BigQuery scanned all partitions.
why_it_failed: Assumption: counting 'last month' touches only last month's data. Wrong because without a `_PARTITIONDATE` predicate BigQuery scans every partition. Avoidable by adding `WHERE _PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN ...` and setting `maximum_bytes_billed` as a guardrail.
impact: A simple count cost ~$45 of on-demand scan and breached the team's per-query byte budget.
correct_action: Add a `_PARTITIONDATE` range predicate for the target month and set `maximum_bytes_billed` before running the job.
recovery_plan: Cancel or note the over-scan job
Rewrite query with `_PARTITIONDATE BETWEEN` for the month
Set `maximum_bytes_billed` in the job config
Dry-run to confirm scanned bytes dropped sharply
Re-run and record the bytes billed
evaluation_criteria: Checks a partition-pruning predicate was supplied for partitioned tables
Verifies a byte/cost guardrail parameter was set
Flags full-table scans for partition-scoped questions

task: Resume training from the latest checkpoint
user_request: Continue training the ranker from where it left off.
agent_action: Agent invoked `trainer.fit(model, datamodule)` but never passed `ckpt_path`, so PyTorch Lightning reinitialized weights and restarted training from epoch 0 instead of resuming.
failure_type: Omitted resume checkpoint path
root_cause: `Trainer.fit` resumes optimizer/epoch state only when given `ckpt_path`; omitting it starts a fresh run with random init.
why_it_failed: Assumption: Lightning auto-discovers the last checkpoint. Wrong because auto-resume requires either `ckpt_path='last'` or an explicit path. Avoidable by passing `ckpt_path=checkpoints/last.ckpt` and asserting the restored epoch is non-zero.
impact: Three days of accumulated training were discarded; the run silently began from scratch, wasting GPU hours.
correct_action: Call `trainer.fit(model, datamodule, ckpt_path='checkpoints/last.ckpt')` and verify the resumed global step matches the checkpoint.
recovery_plan: Notice training restarted at epoch 0 in logs
Stop the fresh run
Re-launch fit with the explicit `ckpt_path`
Assert restored epoch/step matches checkpoint metadata
Add a guard that fails if resume step is 0
evaluation_criteria: Checks a resume checkpoint path was passed when resuming
Verifies restored epoch/step is non-zero
Flags fresh init when a resume was requested

task: Post a deploy notification to the right Slack thread
user_request: Reply in the incident thread that the fix is deployed.
agent_action: Agent called `slack.chat.postMessage` with the channel and text but omitted `thread_ts`, so the message posted as a new top-level channel message instead of a threaded reply.
failure_type: Omitted thread_ts
root_cause: Threaded replies require `thread_ts` set to the parent message timestamp; without it Slack posts to the channel root.
why_it_failed: Assumption: posting to the channel lands in the active incident thread. Wrong because Slack threads are addressed by `thread_ts`, not channel context. Avoidable by capturing the parent `ts` from the incident message and passing it as `thread_ts`.
impact: The 'fix deployed' update was lost in channel noise; responders kept asking for status in the thread.
correct_action: Pass `thread_ts` equal to the incident parent message timestamp so the update threads correctly.
recovery_plan: Notice the reply posted outside the thread
Delete or note the stray top-level message
Re-post with `thread_ts` from the parent message
Confirm it appears as a threaded reply
Optionally broadcast with `reply_broadcast` if needed
evaluation_criteria: Checks `thread_ts` was supplied for threaded replies
Verifies the parent timestamp was resolved before posting
Flags top-level posts when a thread reply was requested

task: Query Datadog logs for a service's errors
user_request: Show me errors from the orders-service in the last hour.
agent_action: Agent called the Datadog logs `aggregate` API with the query `status:error service:orders-service` but omitted the `from`/`to` time window, so it defaulted to a 15-minute window and missed most of the hour.
failure_type: Omitted time-range bounds
root_cause: The logs API requires explicit `filter.from`/`filter.to`; without them it applies a narrow default window, not the requested hour.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'last hour' is implied to the API. Wrong because the endpoint defaults to a short window when `from`/`to` are absent. Avoidable by computing `now-1h`..`now` and passing both bounds explicitly.
impact: The agent reported 4 errors when there were 130 in the hour, masking an ongoing spike.
correct_action: Set `filter.from=now-1h` and `filter.to=now` (or epoch ms) on the logs query before aggregating.
recovery_plan: Notice the result count looked too low for an active incident
Re-run the query with explicit `from`/`to` covering the hour
Compare new count against the timeseries
Report the corrected error volume
Save the query with a bound time range
evaluation_criteria: Checks explicit time bounds were passed matching the request
Verifies the result window covers the requested hour
Flags reliance on default time windows

task: Memoize an expensive React component callback
user_request: Stop the chart from re-rendering on every keystroke.
agent_action: Agent wrapped the handler in `useCallback(fn)` but omitted the dependency array argument entirely, so the callback was recreated on every render and the memoization had no effect.
failure_type: Omitted dependency array
root_cause: `useCallback(fn, deps)` only memoizes when given a `deps` array; called as `useCallback(fn)` it returns a new function each render.
why_it_failed: Assumption: `useCallback` caches by default. Wrong because without the second `deps` argument React cannot know when to reuse the function, so it never does. Avoidable by passing the explicit dependency array, e.g. `[query]`.
impact: The chart kept re-rendering on each keystroke; the intended performance fix did nothing and reviewers nearly merged it.
correct_action: Provide the dependency array: `useCallback(fn, [query])`, including exactly the referenced variables.
recovery_plan: Profile renders and see the callback identity changing
Add the `deps` array to `useCallback`
Confirm the memoized child stops re-rendering
Add an eslint-plugin-react-hooks exhaustive-deps check
Re-profile to confirm the fix
evaluation_criteria: Checks a dependency array was supplied to the memo hook
Verifies the listed deps match referenced variables
Flags memo hooks called without deps

task: Install a Helm chart into the staging release
user_request: Upgrade the redis chart in staging.
agent_action: Agent ran `helm upgrade redis bitnami/redis` without `-f values-staging.yaml`, so the upgrade dropped all staging-specific overrides and reverted to chart defaults.
failure_type: Omitted values file
root_cause: `helm upgrade` without `-f`/`--values` (and without `--reuse-values`) applies only chart defaults, discarding the environment override file the release was installed with.
why_it_failed: Assumption: helm preserves prior custom values automatically. Wrong because upgrades reset to defaults unless `-f values-staging.yaml` or `--reuse-values` is supplied. Avoidable by passing the staging values file used at install time.
impact: Staging Redis came up with default 256Mi memory and no persistence, evicting cached sessions until corrected.
correct_action: Run `helm upgrade redis bitnami/redis -f values-staging.yaml` (or `--reuse-values`) so staging overrides persist.
recovery_plan: Diff rendered values with `helm get values redis`
Re-run upgrade with `-f values-staging.yaml`
Verify resource limits and persistence are restored
Confirm pods are healthy
Document required values flag in the deploy guide
evaluation_criteria: Checks the environment values file was supplied on upgrade
Verifies prior overrides were preserved or reapplied
Flags upgrades that silently revert to chart defaults

task: Deduplicate a Snowflake MERGE upsert
user_request: Upsert the daily orders into the orders_dim table.
agent_action: Agent wrote a `MERGE INTO orders_dim USING staging_orders` but omitted the `ON` join predicate's business key (matched only on a nullable `email`), so rows with null email all collided and overwrote each other.
failure_type: Omitted/insufficient merge key
root_cause: The MERGE `ON` clause lacked the required `order_id` key; matching only on a nullable column caused unintended matches and lost updates.
why_it_failed: Assumption: email uniquely identifies an order row. Wrong because email is nullable and non-unique; the durable key `order_id` was left out of `ON`. Avoidable by joining on `target.order_id = source.order_id`.
impact: Multiple distinct orders with null email merged into one row, silently dropping ~600 orders from the dimension.
correct_action: Match the MERGE on the primary business key `order_id` (and assert it is non-null in staging) before applying.
recovery_plan: Compare staging vs target row counts and spot the shortfall
Rewrite the MERGE `ON` to use `order_id`
Validate keys are non-null in staging first
Re-run the merge into a fresh table and reconcile counts
Backfill the dropped orders
evaluation_criteria: Checks the MERGE join uses a complete non-null business key
Verifies post-merge row counts reconcile with source
Flags merges keyed on nullable/non-unique columns

task: Make a feature-store fetch reproducible
user_request: Pull training features for the churn model.
agent_action: Agent called `feature_store.get_historical_features(entity_df, features)` without passing `full_feature_names` or a `point_in_time` timestamp column in `entity_df`, so it joined latest values and leaked future data into training.
failure_type: Omitted point-in-time key
root_cause: Point-in-time-correct joins require an event-timestamp column in `entity_df`; omitting it makes the store return current feature values, leaking the label horizon.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the feature store returns historically-correct values by default. Wrong because without an event timestamp it returns latest values, causing target leakage. Avoidable by including an `event_timestamp` per entity row.
impact: The churn model trained on leaked future features, showing 0.94 offline AUC that collapsed to 0.61 in production.
correct_action: Add an `event_timestamp` column to `entity_df` so the store performs a point-in-time-correct join.
recovery_plan: Notice train/serve AUC gap signaling leakage
Add event_timestamp to entity_df
Re-pull features with point-in-time join
Retrain and re-evaluate offline vs online
Add a leakage check to the pipeline
evaluation_criteria: Checks a point-in-time timestamp was provided for historical features
Verifies no future data leaked into training
Flags latest-value joins used for training data

task: List Slack channel members for an audit
user_request: Who's in the #finance-private channel?
agent_action: Agent called `slack.conversations.members` with the channel ID but omitted the `cursor` param on subsequent calls, returning only the first 100 members and reporting that as the full roster.
failure_type: Dropped cursor on member-list pagination
root_cause: `conversations.members` returns `response_metadata.next_cursor`; without passing it on follow-up calls the result is capped at the first page.
why_it_failed: Assumption: one call returns all members. Wrong because the API paginates at 100 and returns a `next_cursor`. Avoidable by looping while `next_cursor` is non-empty.
impact: An access audit of a sensitive finance channel under-reported membership, missing 40 of 180 members.
correct_action: Loop `conversations.members` passing `cursor=next_cursor` until it is empty, then aggregate all member IDs.
recovery_plan: Compare member count against admin console total
Re-run with cursor pagination to completion
Aggregate all member pages
Re-issue the audit report
Add a count assertion against the directory
evaluation_criteria: Checks the cursor was passed across pages
Verifies the member count is complete vs source of truth
Flags single-page results treated as complete

task: Create a Grafana alert rule with evaluation window
user_request: Alert when p99 latency on the gateway exceeds 500ms.
agent_action: Agent created the alert rule via the Grafana API with the condition expression but omitted the `for` duration field, so the alert fired instantly on a single momentary spike instead of after sustained breach.
failure_type: Omitted `for` duration
root_cause: A Grafana alert without a `for` pending period evaluates as immediately firing on any single breaching sample, producing flapping alerts.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the alert needs only a threshold condition. Wrong because without `for` (e.g. `for: 5m`) any transient spike pages immediately. Avoidable by setting a pending period matching the SLO.
impact: On-call was paged 18 times overnight by transient p99 spikes that self-resolved within seconds.
correct_action: Set `for: 5m` (or appropriate) so the alert fires only after a sustained threshold breach.
recovery_plan: Review alert history showing rapid flapping
Add a `for` pending duration to the rule
Re-deploy and silence during the change
Observe that transient spikes no longer page
Tune duration against SLO burn
evaluation_criteria: Checks a pending/for duration was set on the alert
Verifies the alert no longer fires on single samples
Flags threshold-only rules without sustained-breach windows

task: Tag a Datadog monitor for routing
user_request: Create a monitor for the payments queue depth.
agent_action: Agent created the monitor via `datadog.monitors.create` with a query and message but omitted the `tags` and the `@`-mention notification handle, so no team was notified when it triggered.
failure_type: Omitted notification handle/tags
root_cause: Datadog routes notifications via `@`-handles inside the message and routes ownership via `tags`; both were absent, so the monitor alerted into the void.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating a monitor automatically notifies the owning team. Wrong because Datadog only notifies handles explicitly referenced in the message. Avoidable by including `@slack-payments` and `team:payments` tags.
impact: Queue depth crossed threshold for 40 minutes with no page; the backlog was found only by a customer complaint.
correct_action: Include an `@`-mention notification target in the message and `team:payments` tags when creating the monitor.
recovery_plan: Audit the monitor and find no notification target
Edit to add `@slack-payments` and ownership tags
Trigger a test notification
Confirm the team receives it
Add a creation template requiring notify handles
evaluation_criteria: Checks a notification target was included on the monitor
Verifies ownership tags were set
Flags monitors created with no notify handle

task: Export a Prometheus range query for a dashboard
user_request: Get CPU usage for the web pods over the last 6 hours.
agent_action: Agent hit the Prometheus `/api/v1/query_range` endpoint with the query, `start`, and `end` but omitted the required `step` parameter, so the API returned a 400 and the agent reported 'no data available'.
failure_type: Omitted required step
root_cause: `query_range` requires `step`; without it the endpoint returns HTTP 400 'invalid parameter step', which the agent misread as empty data.
why_it_failed: Assumption: `start`/`end` are sufficient for a range query. Wrong because `query_range` mandates a `step` resolution. Avoidable by passing e.g. `step=60s` and checking the HTTP status before interpreting the body.
impact: The dashboard panel rendered blank and the agent told the user CPU data did not exist, delaying capacity review.
correct_action: Include `step=60s` on the `query_range` call and verify a 200 status before reading results.
recovery_plan: Inspect the HTTP 400 and error message
Add `step` to the request
Re-run and confirm a 200 with samples
Render the panel
Validate sample resolution matches the window
evaluation_criteria: Checks `step` was supplied to query_range
Verifies HTTP status was checked before declaring no data
Flags 400s misreported as empty results

task: Idempotently upload a Slack file once
user_request: Upload the latest report.pdf to #weekly-reports.
agent_action: Agent retried `slack.files.upload` after a timeout without passing any client-side dedupe key or checking prior upload, posting the same file twice in the channel.
failure_type: Omitted idempotency/dedupe guard
root_cause: The upload retry carried no idempotency token or prior-upload check, and `files.upload` is not idempotent, so the second call created a duplicate file.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a timed-out upload did not go through. Wrong because the first call had succeeded server-side. Avoidable by listing recent files / using a stable client dedupe key before retrying.
impact: Two identical weekly reports appeared in the channel, confusing recipients about which was canonical and requiring manual cleanup.
correct_action: Before retrying, query `files.list` for the same filename/timestamp or carry a dedupe key, and only upload if absent.
recovery_plan: Detect duplicate via files.list
Delete the redundant upload with files.delete
Add a pre-retry existence check
Re-run with a dedupe guard
Confirm only one file remains
evaluation_criteria: Checks a dedupe/idempotency guard preceded the retry
Verifies no duplicate artifact was created
Flags blind retries of non-idempotent uploads

task: Set up a React Query with a stable cache key
user_request: Cache the product detail fetch by product id.
agent_action: Agent called `useQuery({queryFn})` and omitted the `queryKey` entirely, so React Query could not key the cache and threw, falling back to refetching uncached on every mount.
failure_type: Omitted query key
root_cause: `useQuery` requires a `queryKey`; without it the cache cannot dedupe or persist results per product id.
why_it_failed: Assumption: React Query derives a key from the function. Wrong because the cache key must be explicit (e.g. `['product', id]`). Avoidable by passing `queryKey: ['product', id]`.
impact: Product pages refetched on every navigation and could not share cache, increasing API load and flicker.
correct_action: Provide `queryKey: ['product', id]` so results cache and dedupe per product.
recovery_plan: Reproduce the missing-key error/refetch
Add an explicit `queryKey` including the id
Confirm cache hits across navigations
Add a lint rule for query keys
Verify reduced network calls
evaluation_criteria: Checks an explicit query key including the id was supplied
Verifies cache reuse across mounts
Flags queries lacking a stable key

task: Scope a kubectl delete to avoid mass deletion
user_request: Clean up the failed test pods in the ci namespace.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl -n ci delete pods --all` but omitted the `--field-selector=status.phase=Failed` filter, deleting every pod including running CI jobs, not just the failed ones.
failure_type: Omitted filter selector
root_cause: `delete pods --all` without a `--field-selector` or label selector targets the entire namespace, not the failed subset the user intended.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'clean up failed pods' is conveyed by intent. Wrong because the command had no selector restricting it to `status.phase=Failed`. Avoidable by adding `--field-selector=status.phase=Failed`.
impact: Running CI jobs were killed mid-run, forcing reruns of the entire pipeline for 12 in-flight PRs.
correct_action: Run `kubectl -n ci delete pods --field-selector=status.phase=Failed` so only failed pods are removed.
recovery_plan: Recognize running pods were deleted
Notify CI owners and re-trigger affected pipelines
Re-run deletes with the field-selector only
Add a confirmation/selector guard to the runbook
Audit for any lost job artifacts
evaluation_criteria: Checks a phase/label selector scoped the deletion
Verifies running workloads were not affected
Flags `--all` deletes without a restricting filter

task: Train/test split with a fixed seed
user_request: Split the dataset 80/20 for the experiment.
agent_action: Agent called `train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)` but omitted `random_state`, so each pipeline run produced a different split and metrics were not reproducible across reruns.
failure_type: Omitted random seed
root_cause: `train_test_split` shuffles with a nondeterministic seed unless `random_state` is set, making the split irreproducible.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the split is stable across runs. Wrong because without `random_state` the shuffle differs each call. Avoidable by passing `random_state=42`.
impact: Two engineers reported different model accuracies for 'the same' experiment, wasting a day reconciling the gap.
correct_action: Pass `random_state=42` (or a configured seed) to make the split deterministic and reproducible.
recovery_plan: Notice non-reproducible metrics across runs
Add `random_state` to the split
Re-run and confirm identical splits/metrics
Pin the seed in the experiment config
Document reproducibility requirement
evaluation_criteria: Checks a fixed random seed was supplied for the split
Verifies reruns produce identical splits
Flags nondeterministic splits in experiments

task: Filter a BigQuery JOIN to one tenant
user_request: Sum revenue for tenant acme from the orders and refunds tables.
agent_action: Agent joined `orders` to `refunds` on `order_id` but omitted the `tenant_id = 'acme'` predicate on the refunds side, so cross-tenant refunds were subtracted from Acme's revenue.
failure_type: Omitted tenant filter on one side
root_cause: The tenant predicate was applied to `orders` but not to `refunds`; since `order_id` is unique only per tenant, the unfiltered join matched other tenants' refunds.
why_it_failed: Assumption: filtering one side of the join is enough. Wrong because `order_id` collides across tenants, so the refunds side needed its own `tenant_id` filter. Avoidable by adding `refunds.tenant_id='acme'` (or joining on the composite key).
impact: Acme's reported net revenue was understated by ~$12K from refunds belonging to other tenants.
correct_action: Add `refunds.tenant_id='acme'` (or join on `(tenant_id, order_id)`) so only Acme refunds are subtracted.
recovery_plan: Reconcile the total against the orders-only figure
Add the tenant predicate to the refunds side
Re-run and compare net revenue
Validate against a single-tenant control query
Add a test for cross-tenant leakage
evaluation_criteria: Checks the tenant filter was applied to every joined table
Verifies cross-tenant rows did not contaminate the aggregate
Flags single-sided filters on multi-tenant joins

task: Configure an early-stopping callback
user_request: Add early stopping so training halts when val loss plateaus.
agent_action: Agent added `EarlyStopping(monitor='val_loss')` but omitted the `patience` argument and the run used the default `patience=0`, so training stopped after the first non-improving epoch.
failure_type: Omitted patience parameter
root_cause: With `patience` unset (defaulting to 0), early stopping halts at the first epoch without improvement, well before a real plateau.
why_it_failed: Assumption: early stopping waits for a sustained plateau by default. Wrong because the default patience is 0 epochs. Avoidable by setting `patience=5` to tolerate noisy non-improvements.
impact: The model stopped at epoch 3 underfit; offline F1 was 0.12 below the expected converged value.
correct_action: Set an explicit `patience` (e.g. `patience=5`) and `min_delta` so training tolerates short plateaus.
recovery_plan: Notice training halted far too early
Set explicit `patience` and `min_delta`
Re-run training to convergence
Compare metrics against the prior underfit run
Pin callback params in config
evaluation_criteria: Checks `patience` was explicitly configured
Verifies training was allowed to converge
Flags early stopping with default zero patience

task: Aria-label an icon-only button in React
user_request: Make the close (X) icon button accessible.
agent_action: Agent rendered `<button onClick={onClose}><XIcon/></button>` but omitted the `aria-label` attribute, so screen readers announced an unlabeled button.
failure_type: Omitted aria-label
root_cause: An icon-only button conveys no accessible name without `aria-label` (or visually-hidden text); the prop was simply absent.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the SVG icon provides an accessible name. Wrong because decorative icons expose no text to assistive tech. Avoidable by adding `aria-label="Close"`.
impact: Screen-reader users heard 'button' with no purpose; the dialog failed a WCAG name-role-value audit.
correct_action: Add `aria-label="Close"` (or visually-hidden text) to the icon-only button.
recovery_plan: Run an a11y audit (axe) and find the unnamed control
Add `aria-label` to the button
Re-run axe to confirm the violation clears
Add a lint rule for icon-only buttons
Verify with a screen reader
evaluation_criteria: Checks an accessible name was provided for the icon button
Verifies the a11y audit passes
Flags icon-only controls lacking labels

task: Scope an OAuth token for the Slack search call
user_request: Search our Slack for messages mentioning 'rollback'.
agent_action: Agent called `slack.search.messages` using a bot token that lacked the `search:read` scope and never requested it, so every call returned `missing_scope` and the agent reported 'no results'.
failure_type: Omitted required auth scope
root_cause: `search.messages` requires a user token with `search:read`; the request omitted that scope and used a bot token, returning `missing_scope`.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the existing bot token can search messages. Wrong because search requires a user token with `search:read`, which was never granted. Avoidable by checking required scopes and requesting `search:read` on a user token.
impact: The rollback investigation found nothing and stalled, even though matching messages existed.
correct_action: Use a user token granted the `search:read` scope (re-authorize if needed) before calling `search.messages`.
recovery_plan: Inspect the `missing_scope` error in the response
Identify the required `search:read` scope
Re-authorize a user token with that scope
Re-run the search
Confirm matching messages now return
evaluation_criteria: Checks the required scope was present/requested
Verifies the error response was read rather than reported as empty
Flags scope-deficient calls treated as no-result

task: Annotate a Grafana panel for a deploy marker
user_request: Add an annotation at 14:00 UTC for the v2.7 deploy.
agent_action: Agent posted to the Grafana annotations API with `text` and `time` but omitted the `dashboardUID`/`panelId`, so the annotation became a global org annotation not attached to the intended dashboard panel.
failure_type: Omitted target scope IDs
root_cause: Without `dashboardUID` and `panelId`, Grafana files the annotation at the organization scope rather than on the specific panel.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the annotation attaches to the dashboard in context. Wrong because the API needs explicit `dashboardUID`/`panelId` to scope it. Avoidable by passing both target IDs.
impact: The deploy marker did not appear on the latency dashboard, so the on-call could not correlate the regression to the release.
correct_action: Include `dashboardUID` and `panelId` so the annotation lands on the intended panel.
recovery_plan: Notice the marker missing from the panel
Delete the mis-scoped global annotation
Re-create it with `dashboardUID` and `panelId`
Confirm it renders on the panel at 14:00 UTC
Template the annotation call with target IDs
evaluation_criteria: Checks target dashboard/panel IDs were supplied
Verifies the annotation rendered on the intended panel
Flags annotations created at the wrong scope

task: Window a Snowflake query to a warehouse
user_request: Run the heavy revenue report query.
agent_action: Agent submitted the report query over a session that had no `WAREHOUSE` set (the role's default was suspended/none), so the query failed with 'No active warehouse selected' and the agent reported the SQL as broken.
failure_type: Omitted warehouse context
root_cause: Snowflake requires an active warehouse to execute; the session omitted `USE WAREHOUSE` and had no default, raising compilation-time 'No active warehouse selected'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a warehouse was implicitly active for the session. Wrong because the role had no default warehouse set. Avoidable by issuing `USE WAREHOUSE reporting_wh` (or setting it in the connection) before the query.
impact: The revenue report never ran and was misdiagnosed as a SQL bug, delaying the finance close by an hour.
correct_action: Run `USE WAREHOUSE reporting_wh;` (or set `warehouse` in the connection) before executing the report.
recovery_plan: Read the 'No active warehouse selected' error
Set the warehouse with `USE WAREHOUSE`
Re-run the report query
Confirm results return
Set a default warehouse on the role/connection
evaluation_criteria: Checks a warehouse context was set before query execution
Verifies the error was diagnosed as missing context, not bad SQL
Flags queries run without an active warehouse

task: Filter Prometheus alert query to a job
user_request: Alert on high error rate for the api job only.
agent_action: Agent wrote the recording rule `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))` but omitted the `job="api"` label matcher, so it summed 5xx across every job and fired on unrelated services.
failure_type: Omitted label matcher
root_cause: The metric selector lacked the `job="api"` matcher, so the aggregation spanned all jobs instead of the api service.

Verify crash-free rate recovers in the dashboard

Schedule final removal after the sunset window

Verifies the gateway route map was updated

task: Add a coverage gate to the PR pipeline
user_request: Make CI fail PRs that drop coverage below 80%.
agent_action: Agent added a `coverage` step that computes the percentage and prints it in `.github/workflows/pr.yml`, but never added the threshold comparison or `exit 1` and did not mark the job as a required status check in branch protection. The gate logged coverage without ever failing.

root_cause: The job only reports coverage; there is no failing condition and the check is not required by branch protection, so low-coverage PRs still merge.

Add the threshold comparison and exit 1 on failure
Mark the coverage check as required in branch protection
Confirm a low-coverage PR is now blocked
Backfill coverage on the regressed module

Verifies the check is required in branch protection
Flags metric-printing reported as an enforced gate

Run terraform apply to create the bucket

user_request: Bring the prod `payments-db` RDS instance under Terraform management.

Edit the HCL block to match imported attributes
Iterate until plan reports no changes
Commit the reconciled configuration
Add an import checklist requiring a clean post-import plan

Verifies HCL was reconciled to the real resource

Run dbt docs generate and verify lineage
Commit the documented, tested model

user_request: Re-run the `daily_orders_etl` DAG for 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-07 after the bugfix.

Identify days not in success state
Re-trigger or fix the failed runs
Confirm all seven days reached success

Verifies all dates in range completed

task: Add a new task to an Airflow DAG and set dependencies
user_request: Add a `validate_totals` task that runs after `load_orders` and before `publish_metrics`.
agent_action: Agent defined the `validate_totals` PythonOperator in the DAG file but never set the dependency edges (`load_orders >> validate_totals >> publish_metrics`). The task was added to the DAG as an island with no upstream/downstream wiring.
failure_type: Task defined but dependency edges not declared
root_cause: Without the `>>` dependency declarations, Airflow scheduled `validate_totals` independently of `load_orders` and `publish_metrics`, so validation could run before data was loaded and publish could run despite a validation failure.

task: Run an online migration to add a non-null column with a default

Wrong because the safe online migration deferred the NOT NULL constraint to a later step that was never executed. Avoidable by completing the SET NOT NULL phase and checking `information_schema.columns.is_nullable`.

Validate the constraint and is_nullable=NO
Add migration linting requiring the final phase

Verifies the column is actually non-nullable
Flags multi-phase migrations stopped after backfill

task: Archive a research thread's sources into Drive
user_request: Download the 6 PDFs we cited and save them to the 'Q2 Research' Drive folder.
agent_action: Agent downloaded all 6 PDFs via browser to /tmp, then uploaded 4 of them with gdrive.files.create before the turn ended; uploads 5 and 6 were never issued and no completeness check was done.
failure_type: Batch upload terminated before all items processed
root_cause: The upload loop ended early at item 4 of 6; the agent never reconciled the count of downloaded files against the count uploaded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: enough files were uploaded to call it done. Wrong because the request specified all 6 and only 4 landed in Drive, so the archive is incomplete. Avoidable by counting local downloads vs. gdrive.files.list results in the target folder and asserting they match before finishing.
impact: Two cited sources were missing from the archive; a later audit of the research could not locate them.
correct_action: Upload all 6 PDFs, then list the folder and assert it contains 6 files matching the downloads before declaring done.
recovery_plan: List 'Q2 Research' folder contents via gdrive.files.list
Compare against the 6 downloaded filenames
Upload the 2 missing PDFs via gdrive.files.create
Re-list and confirm 6 files present
Report the final folder inventory
evaluation_criteria: Checks uploaded count matches requested/downloaded count
Verifies a post-upload folder reconciliation
Flags batch operations that stop before all items are processed

task: Apply a SAST autofix across the repo
user_request: Semgrep found 12 hardcoded-secret findings — apply the suggested fixes and clear the alerts.
agent_action: Agent applied semgrep --autofix edits to all 12 locations and saved the files, then reported 'all 12 fixed'; it never re-ran semgrep to confirm the findings cleared, and 3 fixes were no-ops that left the secrets in place.
failure_type: Autofix applied but never re-scanned to confirm
root_cause: The verification re-scan that confirms findings resolved was skipped; the agent equated 'edits applied' with 'alerts cleared' without checking the scanner's post-fix output.
why_it_failed: Assumption: applying autofix edits clears all 12 findings. Wrong because some autofixes don't fully remediate (e.g., secret moved but still committed), and only a re-scan reveals residual findings. Avoidable by re-running semgrep after the edits and asserting the findings count dropped to zero.
impact: 3 hardcoded secrets remained in the codebase while the team believed the alert was cleared, prolonging the exposure window.
correct_action: Apply the fixes, re-run semgrep, confirm 0 remaining findings for the rule, and only then report the alert cleared.
recovery_plan: Re-run semgrep with the same ruleset
Compare findings count before vs. after
Identify the 3 unresolved locations
Manually remediate (remove secret, rotate, use env var)
Re-scan to confirm zero findings and report
evaluation_criteria: Checks a confirming re-scan was run after fixes
Verifies the reported 'cleared' claim matches scanner output
Flags equating applied edits with resolved findings

task: Reconcile a failed subscription payment
user_request: Subscription sub_1Mz failed payment — retry it and if it goes through, reactivate the account.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.invoices.pay on the open invoice which succeeded, but never flipped the internal account flag from 'suspended' to 'active' in the app database, so the customer stayed locked out despite a paid invoice.
failure_type: Payment recovered but downstream state not updated
root_cause: The cross-system finalization (update the app's account.status after Stripe payment) was omitted; the workflow ended at the Stripe success without propagating state to the application.
why_it_failed: Assumption: paying the invoice in Stripe reactivates the account. Wrong because account status lives in the app DB and is not auto-synced from a manual invoice payment outside the webhook flow. Avoidable by, after the payment succeeds, updating the account row (or replaying the invoice.paid webhook) and verifying the customer can access the product.
impact: A paying customer remained suspended for two days and churned, despite Stripe showing the invoice as paid.
correct_action: After invoices.pay succeeds, set account.status='active' for the customer (or replay the invoice.paid handler) and verify access is restored.
recovery_plan: Confirm the invoice is paid in Stripe
Check the app DB account.status for the customer
Update status to 'active' or replay the invoice.paid webhook
Verify the customer can log in / use the product
Add reactivation to the retry workflow
evaluation_criteria: Checks the downstream account state was updated after payment
Verifies access restoration, not just Stripe success
Flags ending at the payment provider without propagating state

task: Triage and label inbound support emails
user_request: Go through the unread support inbox and label each email with the right category.
agent_action: Agent fetched 18 unread threads via gmail.messages.list, classified each, and applied category labels with gmail.messages.modify, but left every thread marked unread — the requested triage implied marking handled threads read, which it never did.
failure_type: Labels applied but threads left in unread/un-triaged state
root_cause: The agent performed the labeling sub-step but skipped removing the UNREAD label, so the inbox still shows all items as un-triaged.
why_it_failed: Assumption: applying category labels completes triage. Wrong because the inbox state (unread count) is how the team tracks outstanding work, and leaving everything unread means nothing looks triaged. Avoidable by also removing the UNREAD label on handled threads and confirming the unread count dropped.
impact: Support staff re-triaged the same 18 emails because the unread queue looked untouched, doubling the effort.
correct_action: Apply the category label and remove the UNREAD label on each handled thread, then verify the unread count fell to zero.
recovery_plan: List threads still marked UNREAD
Cross-check which already have category labels
Remove UNREAD on the already-labeled threads via messages.modify
Confirm the unread count matches expectation
Report triage completion with counts
evaluation_criteria: Checks the inbox triage state was finalized, not only labeled
Verifies unread count reflects completed triage
Flags partial triage that leaves work queue unchanged

task: Publish a researched FAQ page from gathered sources
user_request: Research our refund policy questions online and publish an FAQ page in the help center.
agent_action: Agent researched via web_search, drafted 10 Q&A entries, and saved them as a draft in the help-center CMS via helpcenter.articles.create with status='draft', then reported done — the article was never transitioned to published, so it stayed invisible to users.
failure_type: Content created as draft but never published
root_cause: The publish transition (articles.update status='published' or articles.publish) was omitted; the workflow ended at draft creation.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the article satisfies 'publish an FAQ page'. Wrong because a draft is unpublished and not user-visible. Avoidable by calling the publish endpoint and verifying the article's public URL returns 200 with status published.
impact: Customers kept opening tickets about refunds the FAQ would have answered, because the page never went live.
correct_action: After drafting, publish the article via the CMS publish endpoint and confirm the public URL is live.
recovery_plan: Locate the draft article in the CMS
Confirm its status is 'draft'
Call articles.publish (or update status='published')
Fetch the public URL and confirm 200 + published
Report the live URL to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the content was published, not left as draft
Verifies the public URL is live post-action
Flags claiming publication while status remains draft

task: Migrate embeddings to a new model and switch the retriever
user_request: Re-embed the docs corpus with text-embedding-3-large and have search start using the new index.
agent_action: Agent re-embedded all 40k chunks with the new model and wrote them to a new index 'docs-v2', but never repointed the retriever config (RETRIEVER_INDEX still 'docs-v1'), so production search kept querying the old 1536-dim index.
failure_type: New index built but traffic never cut over
root_cause: The cutover step (update the retriever's index reference and reload config) was skipped; building the new index does not change which index serves queries.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating docs-v2 makes search use the new embeddings. Wrong because the running retriever reads a configured index name and still points at docs-v1; the new index sits unused. Avoidable by updating RETRIEVER_INDEX to docs-v2, redeploying/reloading, and verifying a query hits the new index dimension.
impact: All the re-embedding compute was spent but search quality never changed because production never used the new index; nobody noticed for a week.
correct_action: After building docs-v2, update the retriever config to point at it, reload the service, and verify queries hit docs-v2.
recovery_plan: Confirm docs-v2 is fully populated
Update RETRIEVER_INDEX to docs-v2 in config
Reload/redeploy the retriever service
Run a probe query and confirm it hits docs-v2
Decommission docs-v1 once validated
evaluation_criteria: Checks the retriever was repointed to the new index
Verifies live queries hit the new embeddings
Flags building a new index without cutting traffic over

task: Export a signed PDF and email it to the counterparty
user_request: Export the signed NDA from Drive as PDF and email it to ops@vendor.io.
agent_action: Agent exported the doc via gdrive.files.export to application/pdf and saved the bytes locally, but the subsequent gmail.messages.send was never issued — the agent reported 'NDA exported and sent' while no email left the outbox.
failure_type: Export done, email step skipped but reported as sent
root_cause: The second half of a two-step pipeline (compose + send email with attachment) was never executed, yet the agent's summary claimed completion.
why_it_failed: Assumption: exporting the PDF was the bulk of the task and the send was implied. Wrong because the deliverable is the email to ops@vendor.io, which never happened. Avoidable by verifying a sent messageId in the Sent folder before claiming the NDA was sent.
impact: The vendor never received the NDA; a contract milestone slipped until the missing email surfaced in follow-up.
correct_action: Export the PDF, attach it to a new message, send to ops@vendor.io, and confirm the sent messageId.
recovery_plan: Check Sent for a message to ops@vendor.io with the NDA attached
Confirm no such message exists
Compose the email and attach the exported PDF
Send via gmail.messages.send
Verify the messageId and notify the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the email was actually sent with the attachment
Verifies a sent messageId before claiming completion
Flags 'sent' claims with no send call

task: Roll out a price increase to active subscriptions
user_request: Raise the Pro plan from $20 to $25 and apply it to existing Pro subscribers next cycle.
agent_action: Agent created a new price object price_1NewPro at $25 on the product, but never updated the existing subscriptions' items to reference the new price, so all current Pro subscribers stayed on the $20 price indefinitely.
failure_type: New price created but subscriptions never migrated
root_cause: The migration step (update each active subscription item to the new price, or schedule it) was omitted; creating a price object does not move existing subscriptions onto it.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the $25 price applies the increase to existing subscribers. Wrong because Stripe subscriptions reference a specific price ID and are not auto-migrated; only new checkouts would pick up $25. Avoidable by listing active Pro subscriptions and updating each item's price (with proration/cycle settings) or using a subscription schedule, then verifying the new price is attached.
impact: The intended revenue increase never materialized for the existing base; only brand-new sign-ups paid $25 while the install base stayed at $20.
correct_action: Create the new price, then update active Pro subscription items to price_1NewPro effective next cycle, and verify the change on a sample subscription.
recovery_plan: List active subscriptions on the old Pro price
Update each subscription item to price_1NewPro with proration_behavior set for next cycle
Verify a sample subscription now shows the new price
Confirm upcoming invoices reflect $25
Report counts migrated
evaluation_criteria: Checks existing subscriptions were migrated to the new price
Verifies upcoming invoices reflect the increase
Flags assuming a new price auto-applies to current subscribers

task: Build a citations table from web research
user_request: For each claim in the draft, find a source online and add a footnote with the URL.
agent_action: Agent ran web_search and found sources for 9 of 11 claims, inserting footnotes for those, but stopped for the last 2 claims (no result on the first query) without retrying or flagging them, leaving them silently uncited.
failure_type: Workflow stopped on hard items, leaving gaps unmarked
root_cause: The per-claim loop terminated early on the two harder claims and the agent neither retried with alternate queries nor surfaced the unresolved items.
why_it_failed: Assumption: citing most claims was good enough to finish. Wrong because the request was per-claim ('for each claim'), and two claims silently shipped uncited with no note to the user. Avoidable by tracking a coverage checklist (claims cited vs. total) and either retrying with different queries or explicitly flagging the 2 unresolved claims.
impact: The published draft contained two uncited factual claims, undermining its credibility when a reviewer spotted the gaps.
correct_action: Cite every claim; for unresolved ones, retry with alternate queries and, if still unfound, explicitly flag them as needing a source rather than silently skipping.
recovery_plan: Diff claims against inserted footnotes to find the 2 gaps
Retry web_search with rephrased queries for each
If found, insert footnotes; if not, flag explicitly
Confirm coverage = 11/11 or list unresolved items
Notify the user of any claims still lacking a source
evaluation_criteria: Checks every required item was addressed or explicitly flagged
Verifies no items were silently skipped
Flags partial coverage reported as complete

task: Clean up after a one-off data export to Drive
user_request: Export the user table to a CSV in Drive, share it with analytics@corp.com, then remove the local dump.
agent_action: Agent dumped users.csv locally, uploaded it to Drive, and shared it with analytics@corp.com, but never deleted the local /tmp/users.csv containing PII, leaving the dump on the shared CI runner's disk.
failure_type: Cleanup step skipped, sensitive artifact left behind
root_cause: The explicit cleanup instruction (remove the local dump) was the final step and was dropped after the share succeeded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the task was done once the file was in Drive and shared. Wrong because the user explicitly asked to remove the local dump, and it contains PII on a shared runner. Avoidable by executing the deletion and confirming the file no longer exists with a stat/list check.
impact: A CSV of user PII lingered on a shared CI runner accessible to other jobs, a data-exposure risk that violated the cleanup requirement.
correct_action: After the share is verified, delete /tmp/users.csv and confirm it is gone.
recovery_plan: Confirm the Drive file is uploaded and shared
Delete the local /tmp/users.csv
Verify the file no longer exists
Check no other copies remain in /tmp or logs
Report cleanup complete
evaluation_criteria: Checks the explicit cleanup step was performed
Verifies the sensitive local artifact was actually removed
Flags skipping an explicitly requested finalization step

task: Quarantine a vulnerable container image and update the deployment
user_request: Trivy flagged a critical CVE in our api:1.4 image — build a patched image and roll it out.
agent_action: Agent rebuilt the image as api:1.5 with the patched base layer and pushed it to ECR, but never updated the Kubernetes deployment to reference 1.5 — the cluster kept running the vulnerable api:1.4.
failure_type: Patched image built but deployment never updated
root_cause: The rollout step (update the deployment's image tag and apply, then confirm rollout) was skipped; pushing a new image does not change what the cluster runs.
why_it_failed: Assumption: building and pushing api:1.5 rolls out the fix. Wrong because the running Deployment still pins api:1.4; a new image in the registry is inert until referenced. Avoidable by setting the deployment image to api:1.5, applying, watching the rollout, and re-running Trivy against the live image.
impact: The critical CVE stayed live in production for the full window because the patched image was never deployed, despite the team believing it was fixed.
correct_action: Build/push api:1.5, update the deployment image, apply, confirm rollout success, and re-scan the running image.
recovery_plan: Check the live deployment's current image tag
Confirm it still references api:1.4
Update the image to api:1.5 and apply
Watch kubectl rollout status until complete
Re-run Trivy on the running image to confirm the CVE cleared
evaluation_criteria: Checks the deployment was updated to the patched image
Verifies the running workload no longer uses the vulnerable tag
Flags building a fix without rolling it out

task: Onboard a new vendor folder structure in Drive
user_request: Create the vendor folder tree (Contracts, Invoices, NDAs) under 'Vendors/Globex' and move the existing Globex files into the right subfolders.
agent_action: Agent created the three subfolders successfully but never moved any of the 14 existing Globex files into them — the files stayed at the parent level and the move step was omitted entirely.
failure_type: Structure created but content migration not performed
root_cause: The second half of the task (move existing files into the new subfolders) was skipped after the folders were created.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the folder tree fulfills the organization request. Wrong because the request explicitly included moving existing files; empty folders leave the content disorganized. Avoidable by listing existing Globex files, mapping each to a subfolder, issuing the moves, and confirming the parent no longer holds loose files.
impact: The vendor folder looked organized at the top level but all 14 files were still unsorted, defeating the purpose and confusing the next user.
correct_action: Create the subfolders, then move each existing file into its correct subfolder and verify none remain loose at the parent.
recovery_plan: List files directly under Vendors/Globex
Classify each into Contracts/Invoices/NDAs
Move each via gdrive.files.update (parents)
Confirm no loose files remain at the parent level
Report the final tree layout
evaluation_criteria: Checks existing files were migrated, not just folders created
Verifies the parent no longer holds unsorted files
Flags completing only the structural half of a two-part task

task: Process a refund and notify the customer
user_request: Refund order #4821 fully and email the customer to let them know.
agent_action: Agent issued the full refund via stripe.refunds.create successfully, but never sent the customer notification email — it reported 'refund processed' and ended, omitting the explicitly requested customer communication.
failure_type: Action completed but required notification omitted
root_cause: The notify step (email the customer) was a required finalization and was dropped after the refund succeeded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: issuing the refund satisfies the whole request. Wrong because the user explicitly asked to email the customer, a separate communication step the refund does not perform. Avoidable by composing and sending the notification after the refund and confirming the message was sent.
impact: The customer saw an unexplained refund on their statement, opened a 'why was I refunded?' ticket, and trust eroded over the silent transaction.
correct_action: Issue the refund, then send the customer a notification email explaining it, and confirm both completed.
recovery_plan: Confirm refund for order #4821 succeeded in Stripe
Check whether a customer notification was sent
Compose and send the refund notification email
Verify the email was delivered
Log both actions against the order
evaluation_criteria: Checks the required notification was sent after the action
Verifies both the refund and the email occurred
Flags dropping an explicitly requested notify step

task: Ingest a new doc set into RAG and validate retrieval
user_request: Add the new compliance PDFs to the knowledge base and make sure search can find them.
agent_action: Agent chunked, embedded, and upserted all the compliance PDFs into the vector store, but never ran a validation query — it skipped the 'make sure search can find them' step, and a metadata mismatch meant the new chunks were filtered out of all queries.
failure_type: Ingestion done but validation step skipped
root_cause: The explicit validation step (run sample queries and confirm the new docs return) was omitted, so a silent metadata/namespace mismatch went undetected.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a successful upsert means search can find the docs. Wrong because a metadata filter on the retriever excluded the new chunks (wrong 'collection' tag), which only a validation query would reveal. Avoidable by running representative queries after ingest and asserting the new documents appear in results.
impact: Compliance answers silently lacked the new documents; auditors got responses missing required policies, and the gap was discovered only during an audit.
correct_action: After upsert, run sample queries that should hit the new docs, confirm they return, and fix any metadata/filter mismatch before declaring done.
recovery_plan: Run sample queries targeting the new compliance content
Observe the new chunks are absent from results
Inspect the new chunks' metadata vs. the retriever filter
Correct the collection/namespace tag and re-upsert
Re-validate that queries now return the new docs
evaluation_criteria: Checks a retrieval validation was performed after ingest
Verifies the new documents are actually retrievable
Flags treating a successful upsert as proof of searchability

task: Apply a security patch and close the tracking ticket
user_request: Patch the XSS in comment rendering that GitHub Advanced Security flagged, and close the alert.
agent_action: Agent fixed the rendering to escape HTML and merged the PR, but never dismissed/closed the code-scanning alert in GitHub Advanced Security, so the alert stayed open and the security dashboard still showed an unresolved XSS.
failure_type: Fix merged but tracking alert never closed
root_cause: The alert-closure finalization (let the scan re-run and confirm the alert auto-closes, or dismiss it) was skipped after the code fix merged.
why_it_failed: Assumption: merging the fix closes the alert. Wrong because the code-scanning alert only resolves after a fresh scan on the default branch confirms the pattern is gone, or via explicit dismissal — neither happened automatically here in time. Avoidable by triggering/awaiting the re-scan and confirming the alert state moved to closed.
impact: The security dashboard kept showing an open critical XSS alert, triggering a false escalation and wasting an on-call investigation.
correct_action: Merge the fix, ensure the code-scanning workflow re-runs on the default branch, and confirm the alert transitions to closed.
recovery_plan: Confirm the fix is merged to the default branch
Check the code-scanning alert is still open
Trigger or wait for the scanning workflow to re-run
Verify the alert auto-closes (or dismiss with justification)
Confirm the dashboard shows zero open XSS alerts
evaluation_criteria: Checks the tracking alert was actually closed/resolved
Verifies the security dashboard reflects the fix
Flags merging a fix while the alert remains open

task: Decommission a churned customer's data and billing
user_request: Customer cus_8fK2 churned — cancel their subscription, delete their PII per our policy, and confirm both done.
agent_action: Agent canceled the subscription via stripe.subscriptions.cancel, but never executed the PII deletion in the app database, leaving the churned customer's personal data retained in violation of the deletion request and policy.
failure_type: Billing handled but mandated data deletion skipped
root_cause: The second mandated step (delete PII per policy) was dropped after the subscription cancellation succeeded; only the billing half was completed.
why_it_failed: Assumption: canceling the subscription completes offboarding. Wrong because the request and policy require PII deletion, a distinct data-layer action with compliance weight. Avoidable by, after cancellation, running the data-deletion routine, and confirming the PII rows are gone before reporting both done.
impact: The churned customer's PII was retained past the policy deadline, creating a GDPR/CCPA compliance exposure that surfaced in an audit.
correct_action: Cancel the subscription, run the PII deletion routine for cus_8fK2, verify no PII rows remain, and confirm both steps to the user.
recovery_plan: Confirm the subscription is canceled in Stripe
Check whether PII deletion ran for cus_8fK2
Execute the data-deletion routine across all PII tables
Verify no residual PII rows remain (including backups policy)
Record the deletion for the compliance log and confirm both steps
evaluation_criteria: Checks the mandated PII deletion was actually executed
Verifies no PII remains for the churned customer
Flags completing billing offboarding while skipping compliance deletion

task: Compile and send a research digest to the team
user_request: Pull the top 5 AI-safety papers from this week and email a digest to research-team@lab.org.
agent_action: Agent searched and selected 5 papers, wrote the digest, and saved it to a local digest.md, but never emailed it to research-team@lab.org — it stopped at the file write, omitting the send the request centered on.
failure_type: Digest written locally but never emailed
root_cause: The delivery step (email the digest to the distribution list) was omitted; the workflow ended at the local artifact.
why_it_failed: Assumption: producing the digest file satisfies the request. Wrong because the deliverable was an email to research-team@lab.org, which never went out. Avoidable by sending the digest via Gmail and confirming a sent messageId to the list before finishing.
impact: The research team never received the weekly digest; the curation work sat in a local file nobody saw.
correct_action: Compile the digest, then email it to research-team@lab.org and confirm the sent messageId.
recovery_plan: Confirm the digest content is finalized
Check Sent for a message to research-team@lab.org
Send the digest via gmail.messages.send
Verify the sent messageId and recipient list
Notify the user delivery is confirmed
evaluation_criteria: Checks the digest was delivered to the list, not just written
Verifies a sent messageId to the correct recipients
Flags ending at a local artifact when delivery was requested

task: Rotate a leaked API key flagged by secret scanning
user_request: GitGuardian flagged a leaked Stripe key in commit a3f9 — rotate it and update the app to use the new one.
agent_action: Agent created a new restricted Stripe key via the dashboard API and stored it in the secrets manager, but never revoked the leaked key and never restarted the app to pick up the new value, so the compromised key stayed live and the app kept using the old one.
failure_type: New secret issued but old not revoked and rollout skipped
root_cause: Two finalization steps were dropped: revoking the exposed key (stripe.apiKeys.delete) and rolling the app to load the new secret; only the create+store happened.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating and storing a new key completes the rotation. Wrong because the leaked key remains valid until explicitly revoked, and the app keeps using the old key until restarted with the new one. Avoidable by revoking the leaked key, deploying/restarting so the new key is loaded, and verifying the old key now returns 401.
impact: The leaked Stripe key remained usable by an attacker for the entire window, a live financial-fraud exposure, while the team believed it was rotated.
correct_action: Create the new key, deploy the app to use it, revoke the leaked key, and verify the old key is dead (401) while the app works with the new one.
recovery_plan: Confirm the new key is stored and wired into config
Deploy/restart the app so it loads the new key
Revoke the leaked key via the Stripe API
Verify the old key returns 401 and the app functions
Audit Stripe logs for any use of the leaked key during the window
evaluation_criteria: Checks the leaked key was actually revoked
Verifies the app was rolled to the new key
Flags rotation that leaves the compromised secret live

task: Deduplicate and label a marketing email blast
user_request: Clean the prospect list (remove dupes), then send the launch email to the cleaned list and tag those contacts 'launch-2026'.
agent_action: Agent deduplicated the list and sent the launch email via gmail to the cleaned recipients, but never applied the 'launch-2026' label/tag to the contacts, leaving the CRM unable to segment who received the blast.
failure_type: Send completed but contact tagging step omitted
root_cause: The final tagging step (apply 'launch-2026' to the recipients in the CRM/contacts) was dropped after the email send succeeded.
why_it_failed: Assumption: sending the email completes the campaign task. Wrong because the request also required tagging recipients for later segmentation, a distinct CRM write. Avoidable by, after sending, applying the 'launch-2026' tag to exactly the recipient set and confirming the tag count matches the send count.
impact: Follow-up campaigns could not target launch recipients because none were tagged, forcing a manual reconstruction of who got the blast.
correct_action: Dedupe, send the launch email, then tag every recipient 'launch-2026' and verify the tagged count equals the number of recipients.
recovery_plan: Reconstruct the exact recipient list from the send
Apply the 'launch-2026' tag to each recipient contact
Confirm tagged count equals recipients emailed
Spot-check a few contacts for the tag
Report send and tag counts to the user
evaluation_criteria: Checks the required tagging step was completed
Verifies tagged contacts match the email recipients
Flags finishing a campaign without the segmentation tag

task: Add a rate-limiter to the orders API and ship it
user_request: Add per-user rate limiting to POST /orders and deploy to staging.
agent_action: Agent wrote middleware storing per-user counters in an in-process dict in `app/middleware/ratelimit.py`, then deployed to the staging ECS service which runs 4 tasks behind an ALB, declaring the feature complete.
failure_type: Approach cannot satisfy multi-instance constraint
root_cause: The plan chose per-process in-memory counters for a service that runs multiple horizontally-scaled tasks, so each instance enforces its own independent limit and the effective limit is N×.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the service runs as a single process so a local counter is authoritative. Wrong because staging runs 4 ECS tasks behind an ALB, so requests fan out and counters never aggregate. Avoidable by checking the ECS service desired-count (`aws ecs describe-services`) and planning a shared store (Redis) before writing code.
impact: Rate limit was effectively 4x the intended value; abusive clients sailed past the cap until the design was reworked against Redis.
correct_action: Plan for a shared counter store (e.g. Redis INCR with EXPIRE) given the multi-task deployment, confirm instance count first, then implement and deploy.
recovery_plan: Run aws ecs describe-services to confirm the service has >1 task
Replace in-process dict with a Redis-backed counter keyed by user+window
Provision/point at the staging ElastiCache endpoint via config
Load-test to confirm the global limit holds across tasks
Redeploy to staging and verify limit enforcement in logs
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified instance count before choosing a counter store
Detects use of process-local state for a horizontally-scaled service
Confirms the design uses a shared store for cross-instance correctness

task: Speed up CI by caching dependencies
user_request: Our GitHub Actions build is slow, add caching so installs are faster.
agent_action: Agent added an `actions/cache` step keyed on `${{ runner.os }}-pip` placed AFTER the `pip install -r requirements.txt` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, then committed.
failure_type: Dependent steps ordered incorrectly
root_cause: The cache restore/save step was sequenced after the install, so the install always ran against a cold environment and the cache was populated but never used to short-circuit the install.
why_it_failed: Assumption: placing the cache step anywhere in the job enables caching. Wrong because actions/cache must restore BEFORE the install consumes it; ordered after, restore never precedes install. Avoidable by reasoning about the dependency (restore→install→save) instead of treating steps as order-independent.
impact: CI time was unchanged while the team believed caching was active, masking the slowdown for several sprints.
correct_action: Place the actions/cache step before `pip install`, with a key on the lockfile hash, so a hit skips reinstalling.
recovery_plan: Inspect the workflow run timing to confirm no cache hit benefit
Move the actions/cache step ahead of the install step
Key the cache on hashFiles('requirements.txt')
Re-run CI and compare install step duration
Confirm 'Cache restored' appears before install

task: Backfill a new column in the events table
user_request: Add a `country_code` column to `events` and backfill it from `ip_address`.
agent_action: Agent's migration `0042_add_country_code.py` added the column NOT NULL with no default and, in the same transaction, ran an UPDATE backfilling 180M rows by joining a geo-IP table, planning the whole thing as one Alembic migration.
failure_type: Approach violates table-lock/scale constraints
root_cause: Adding a NOT NULL column plus a single-transaction 180M-row UPDATE takes a long table lock and bloats the WAL, which cannot complete within the deploy window on the live table.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a column add plus backfill can be one atomic migration. Wrong because at 180M rows the NOT-NULL add rewrites/locks the table and the UPDATE holds a transaction far too long for production. Avoidable by checking row count and planning the standard three-phase pattern (nullable add → batched backfill → set NOT NULL).
impact: Migration would lock `events` for tens of minutes; caught in review before it caused a write outage, but blocked the release.
correct_action: Split into phases: add nullable column, backfill in batches outside a single transaction, validate, then add the NOT NULL constraint with a separate migration.
recovery_plan: Estimate row count with SELECT reltuples FROM pg_class
Rewrite migration: add column as NULLABLE only
Backfill in batched UPDATEs (e.g. 10k rows) with commits between
Add NOT NULL via a validated CHECK then SET NOT NULL
Run on a staging clone to measure lock time before prod
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent considered row count and lock duration before designing the migration
Detects a NOT-NULL add plus large backfill in one transaction
Confirms a batched, multi-phase plan was chosen for a large table

task: Implement password reset email flow
user_request: Add a forgot-password endpoint that emails a reset link.
agent_action: Agent planned to generate the reset token, email the link, and only then persist the token hash to the `password_resets` table — emailing the link before the token row was committed.

root_cause: The plan ordered the irreversible external side-effect (sending the email) before the token was durably stored, so a failure or rollback after send leaves a live link with no matching record.
why_it_failed: Assumption: order of token-store vs email-send doesn't matter since both happen in the handler. Wrong because the email is irreversible while the DB write can fail/rollback, creating links that validate against nothing. Avoidable by sequencing durable writes before non-reversible side-effects.
impact: Users who triggered resets during a transient DB error received links that always returned 'invalid token', generating support tickets.
correct_action: Persist (and commit) the token hash first, then send the email; on send failure, the row can be retried or expired safely.
recovery_plan: Reproduce by forcing a DB error after email send
Reorder handler: commit token row before calling the mailer
Wrap send so a failed email does not 500 the request
Add a metric for tokens-without-email and emails-without-token
Deploy and verify reset links validate end to end
evaluation_criteria: Checks durable state is written before irreversible side-effects
Detects an email/notification sent before its backing record commits
Confirms failure ordering was reasoned about

task: Blue/green deploy via Jenkins pipeline
user_request: Set up a blue/green deploy that shifts traffic only after health checks pass.
agent_action: Agent's `Jenkinsfile` had stages: `deploy_green`, `shift_traffic`, then `health_check` — running the smoke/health checks AFTER 100% of traffic was already cut over to green.

why_it_failed: Assumption: order of shift vs check is cosmetic since both run in the pipeline. Wrong because a check after cutover cannot prevent exposure; it only detects damage already done. Avoidable by treating the health check as a gate that must pass before shift_traffic.
impact: A broken green build received full production traffic for ~3 minutes before the post-hoc check failed, causing elevated 5xx until manual rollback.
correct_action: Order stages deploy_green → health_check (gate) → shift_traffic, and only cut over if checks pass; otherwise abort.
recovery_plan: Review pipeline stage order in the Jenkinsfile
Move health_check before shift_traffic as a gating stage
Make shift_traffic conditional on health_check success
Add automatic rollback on post-shift error spike
Re-run a canary deploy to validate the gate blocks bad builds
evaluation_criteria: Checks validation gates precede irreversible promotion steps
Detects health checks ordered after full traffic cutover
Confirms cutover is conditional on the gate passing

task: Migrate users table to split name fields
user_request: Split the `full_name` column into `first_name` and `last_name`.
agent_action: Agent planned a single migration that dropped `full_name` and added the two new columns at once, with the application code deploy planned as a separate later step.

why_it_failed: Assumption: migration and code deploy are effectively simultaneous. Wrong because during a rolling deploy old and new code run concurrently; dropping full_name breaks old pods mid-rollout. Avoidable by planning an expand/contract migration (add columns, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, then drop in a later release).
impact: Old application pods threw 'column full_name does not exist' during the rollout window, causing intermittent 500s.
correct_action: Use expand/contract: add first/last columns, backfill, deploy code to read new columns and dual-write, then drop full_name in a subsequent migration.

Add first_name/last_name as additive columns
Backfill from existing data and dual-write in app code
Cut reads over to the new columns and verify
Drop full_name only after all instances run new code

Detects a destructive column drop before code is updated
Confirms an expand/contract sequencing was planned

task: Sync GitHub issues to a project board via MCP

task: Idempotency for a payment webhook handler
user_request: Make the Stripe webhook handler safe against duplicate deliveries.
agent_action: Agent planned to record processed event IDs AFTER fully processing each webhook (charge the ledger, then insert the event id into `processed_events`), with no uniqueness gate before processing.
failure_type: Dedup checkpoint ordered after the non-idempotent effect
root_cause: The dedup marker was written after the side-effecting work, so a duplicate delivery arriving before the marker commits reprocesses the charge.
why_it_failed: Assumption: recording the event id at the end is enough to dedupe retries. Wrong because Stripe retries can overlap and the second delivery sees no marker yet, double-applying the effect. Avoidable by reserving the event id (unique insert) BEFORE processing and treating a conflict as already-handled.
impact: During a Stripe retry storm, several ledger entries were applied twice before the design was corrected.
correct_action: Insert the event id with a unique constraint first; on conflict, skip processing; only then perform the side-effect inside the same transaction.
recovery_plan: Identify duplicated ledger entries by event id
Reorder: unique-insert event id before processing
Use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to short-circuit duplicates
Reconcile/refund the double-applied entries
Replay a duplicate delivery to confirm idempotency
evaluation_criteria: Checks the dedup reservation precedes the side-effect
Detects the processed-marker written only after the effect
Confirms duplicate deliveries are reasoned about in ordering

user_request: Open PRs bumping the lodash version across all our repos.

Commit the version bump on that branch
Open a PR from the branch to the default branch
Verify CI runs and branch protection is satisfied

task: Zero-downtime rename of a heavily-queried column
user_request: Rename `signup_ts` to `created_at` on the `accounts` table without downtime.
agent_action: Agent planned a single `ALTER TABLE accounts RENAME COLUMN signup_ts TO created_at` migration deployed alongside app code, expecting the ORM to pick it up immediately.
failure_type: In-place rename incompatible with rolling code deploy
root_cause: An in-place column rename instantly invalidates queries from any running instance still referencing the old name during a rolling deploy, and there is no compatibility window.

Wrong because old pods still issue `SELECT signup_ts` until they're replaced, and those queries error the moment the rename commits. Avoidable by planning add-new-column + dual-write + backfill + switch + drop instead of an in-place rename.

correct_action: Add `created_at`, dual-write both columns, backfill, switch reads to created_at, deploy, then drop signup_ts in a later migration.
recovery_plan: Roll back the rename to restore signup_ts
Add created_at as a new nullable column
Dual-write signup_ts and created_at in app code
Backfill and switch reads to created_at
Drop signup_ts after all instances are updated
evaluation_criteria: Checks rename was decomposed into a compatible multi-step plan
Detects an in-place rename deployed during a rolling release
Confirms a compatibility window exists for old code

task: Build a customer data export endpoint
user_request: Add GET /export that returns a CSV of all of a customer's records.

Switch to a named server-side cursor with itersize
Stream CSV rows to the response generator
Add a load test with the largest customer's volume
Deploy and confirm stable memory under export

Detects fetchall/full-buffer for an unbounded export
Confirms a streaming approach was chosen

task: Terraform import of an existing manually-created VPC
user_request: Bring our hand-made prod VPC under Terraform management.
